studies.officialTitle: A Randomized, Double-blind, Placebo-controlled Phase II Clinical Study to Evaluate the Efficacy and Safety of IBI362 in Chinese Overweight and Obese Subjects

design.description: Two-stage study sharing one registry identity. Stage 1 (reported with full outcomes below) randomized participants 3:1:3:1:3:1 to mazdutide 3 mg, 4.5 mg, or 6 mg (each dose paired with its own randomized placebo group) for 24 weeks across 20 hospitals in China (n=248). Stage 2 (also reported with full outcomes below; published separately as Ji et al., Med 2026) added a 9 mg cohort restricted to a BMI >=30 kg/m2 subgroup without diabetes, randomized 3:1 (block size 8) to mazdutide 9 mg (titrated 3 mg per 4 weeks to the 9 mg target by week 9) or placebo for 24 weeks at 8 sites (n=80); a voluntary, non-randomized 24-week extension followed for participants who opted in. Stage 1 and Stage 2 "were conducted independently" per the Stage 2 publication's own Methods.

studies.population: Chinese adults aged 18 to 75 years with BMI ≥28 kg/m², or ≥24 kg/m² with at least one of hyperphagia, prediabetes, hypertension, dyslipidemia, fatty liver disease, weight-bearing joint pain, obesity-induced dyspnea, or obstructive sleep apnea syndrome; participants with diabetes mellitus were excluded.
studies.overallDuration: 24 weeks of treatment plus 12 weeks of follow-up
studies.safetySummary: Stage 1 (see per-arm outcomes above). Stage 2 (9 mg, BMI>=30 subgroup, n=60/20): no serious TEAEs and no discontinuations for adverse events in either arm through 24 weeks. Any-grade TEAEs: 95.0% mazdutide vs 80.0% placebo, driven by gastrointestinal events (nausea 50.0% vs 0%; diarrhea 38.3% vs 10.0%; vomiting 36.7% vs 10.0%) and a high background COVID-19 infection rate in both arms (60.0% vs 40.0%) reflecting the pandemic-era enrollment period. Treatment-induced anti-mazdutide antibodies were detected in 28.3% of the mazdutide arm, with no apparent effect on weight-loss efficacy in post hoc analysis.

studies.officialTitle: A Multicenter, Randomized, Open-label Phase 3 Study Comparing the Efficacy and Safety of IBI362 Versus Semaglutide in Chinese Participants With Early Type 2 Diabetes and Obesity (DREAMS-3)

design.description: Open-label, active-comparator head-to-head study randomizing participants to once-weekly mazdutide (titrated up to 9 mg) or once-weekly semaglutide (titrated up to 1.0 mg) for 32 weeks.

studies.population: Chinese adults aged 18 years or older with type 2 diabetes diagnosed within 5 years, HbA1c 7.5-9.5% on diet/exercise with or without stable metformin, and BMI ≥28 kg/m².
studies.safetySummary: Gastrointestinal symptoms were the most common adverse events in both arms, mostly mild to moderate in severity, with no new safety signals identified for mazdutide relative to semaglutide.

studies.officialTitle: Safety and Efficacy of a GLP-1 and Glucagon Receptor Dual Agonist Mazdutide (IBI362) 9 mg and 10 mg in Chinese Adults With Overweight or Obesity: A Randomised, Placebo-controlled, Multiple-ascending-dose Phase 1b Trial

design.description: Multiple-ascending-dose design at five Chinese hospitals; participants randomized 2:1 to mazdutide or placebo within each of a 9 mg cohort (12 weeks) and a 10 mg cohort (16 weeks), each cohort with its own randomized placebo group.

studies.population: Chinese adults aged 18-75 years with overweight (BMI ≥24 kg/m² with hyperphagia and/or at least one obesity-related comorbidity) or obesity (BMI ≥28 kg/m²).
studies.overallDuration: 12 weeks of treatment (9 mg cohort) or 16 weeks of treatment (10 mg cohort)
studies.safetySummary: No serious adverse events were reported. Treatment-emergent adverse events were mild to moderate, led by gastrointestinal symptoms (nausea up to 62.5% in the higher-dose cohort vs 37.5% in the lower-dose cohort; diarrhea 50%; decreased appetite 62.5%; vomiting 37.5%) and a heart-rate increase of up to 17.4 bpm alongside a concurrent blood-pressure decrease.

studies.officialTitle: Efficacy and Safety of IBI362 Versus Dulaglutide as add-on to Metformin and/or SGLT2 Inhibitor or TZD in Subjects With Type 2 Diabetes (DREAMS-2)

design.masking: Dose-blind for mazdutide; open-label active comparator
design.description: Randomized 1:1:1 to once-weekly mazdutide 4 mg, mazdutide 6 mg (dose-blind), or open-label once-weekly dulaglutide 1.5 mg, as add-on to background metformin with or without an SGLT2 inhibitor or sulfonylurea, for 28 weeks, at 71 hospitals in China.

studies.population: Chinese adults aged 18 or older with type 2 diabetes, HbA1c 7.5-11.0% on stable-dose metformin (>=1500 mg/day) alone or combined with an SGLT2 inhibitor or a fixed daily dose of sulfonylureas for at least 2 months, and BMI >=23 kg/m2.
studies.overallDuration: 28 weeks of treatment plus 4-week off-treatment follow-up
studies.safetySummary: TEAE incidence was higher with mazdutide (90.1% with 4 mg, 88.9% with 6 mg) than dulaglutide (82.4%); serious adverse events were balanced (5.8%, 4.9%, 7.8%). One death occurred in the 4 mg mazdutide group (metastatic lung cancer, assessed unrelated to treatment). The most common TEAEs were diarrhoea, decreased appetite, nausea, and vomiting, mostly mild to moderate and concentrated in the dose-escalation period.
